newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: JUNCKER SAYS EMU TO START ON TIME WITH SOUTHERNERS.
newsitem.headline: JUNCKER SAYS EMU TO START ON TIME WITH SOUTHERNERS.

text.p: European Economic and Monetary Union will begin on January 1, 1999 by applying the Maastricht treaty as it stands and including southerners, Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker said on Tuesday.
"I remain convinced that Economic and Monetary Union will, as foreseen, take place on January 1, 1999 on the basis of the Maastricht Treaty convergence criteria," Juncker told a banking seminar.
The Luxembourg Prime Minister who doubles Finance Minister met German Finance Minister Theo Waigel on Monday night.
"After this meeting I remain convinced that Germany will take part...as will France," he said.
Juncker also set about destroying suggestions that the creation of the European Union's single currency would initially only involve the richer northern EU nations.
"It will not be a northern club, but a very significant group that will include countries from the south," he said.
"Not all southern countries will take part, but those that do will be selected according to the treaty criteria.

"We must apply the treaty, the whole treaty and nothing but the treaty...The countries that do not take part in the first wave will not be relegated, but will be able to join when the study of their situations is not dangerous," Juncker added.
Italy in particular is desperate to be in the first wave of nations merging their currencies. The choice will be made early next year. -- Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6810
